extracted.intended_audience: literate general readers of The Spectator / readers of early-18th-century satirical/social essays
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative remarks relevant to composing and judging short satirical/social essays and the social conduct they address (age-appropriate behavior, leadership, parenting, use of allegory, unity in composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances for age-appropriate inclinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Those Ancients ... allotted Inclinations and Objects of Desire particular to every Stage, according to the different Circumstances of our Conversation and Fortune, thro' the several Periods of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indulge the levity of childhood with tenderness; overlook the gaiety of youth with good-nature; temper the forward ambition and impatience of ripen'd manhood with discretion; impute the tenacious avarice of old men to their want of relish for other enjoyment. Maintain decency and regularity in the course of life; dignity suffers when the natural order is inverted and feebleness attempts the outward pomp of youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let sons have lawful diversions proportional to future fortune
rubrics_metrics.description: The Skill therefore should, methinks, be to let a Son want no lawful Diversion, in proportion to his future Fortune, and the Figure he is to make in the World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing appropriate recreation prevents youths of condition from becoming cheats or rascals to supply themselves for debauchery. Allowing sons reasonable expense/spare prevents criminal resourcefulness born of narrowness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide education suitable to social quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The contrary Practice has prevail'd ... I have known them deny them what was merely necessary for Education suitable to their Quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents should supply the means necessary for an education befitting their children's station; denying such resources perverse vanity or stinginess can ruin a son's prospects and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excluding children from society out of vanity
rubrics_metrics.description: A Man may, if he will, let his Heart close to the having no regard to any thing but his dear self, even with exclusion of his very Children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parental affectations of refinement or desire to keep sole memory of possessions should not lead to socially excluding one's children; such behavior is a moral failing and harms family continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as the primary quality for public direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is the first Quality in the Man who is in a Post of Direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good leader decides impartially, becomes a locus for disputes to be laid before him in private, can reconcile animosities by simple command; he should keep records (e.g., dates of commissions), dismiss those deficient in duty, prefer according to merit/order, recommend extraordinary merit for higher distinction, and maintain accountability so each subordinate can answer for what happens in their charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer according to merit and keep business short
rubrics_metrics.description: His Business was very short, and he who had nothing to do but Justice, was never affronted with a Request of a familiar daily Visitant for what was due to a brave Man at a Distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid long, diffuse administration; promote and reward based on merit and order; do not allow private affection to be a step toward preferment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid whimsical distribution of favors / nepotism
rubrics_metrics.description: All the Evils ... have arose from the wanton Disposition of the Favours of the Powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whimsical or self-interested bestowal of favors undermines public order and merit; modesty and virtue must sometimes manoeuvre to penetrate a great man's caprice, but public administration should resist whims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make a practice of delighting in coxcombs and buffoons (leaders)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Leo X. reigned ... his whole Delight was in finding out new Fools, and ... making them shew themselves to advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders who publicly encourage fools or buffoons risk lowering public reverence for office and for institutions; such behavior can teach the populace to mock vestments and signs of authority and ask that authority rest on argument and sanctity of life rather than theatrical display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of public amusement that undermines institutional dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a criminal Humility ... to believe you cannot excel but in the Conversation of Half-wits, Humorists, Coxcombs, and Buffoons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public figures should reflect that habitual jesting or dressing for amusement may erode respect and lead to contempt of sacred or authoritative signs (e.g., caps, gowns), so weigh personal pleasure against institutional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of time and place (literary criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have heard our Criticks in the Coffee-houses hereabout talk mightily of the Unity of Time and Place: According to my Notion of the Matter, I have endeavoured at something like it in the Beginning of my Epistle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The classic dramatic unities (time and place) are a recognized critical standard among contemporary critics; writers of essays/epistles may aim for something like unity to please the critical taste of coffee-house audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory is a valued literary form
rubrics_metrics.description: As some of the finest Compositions among the Ancients are in Allegory, I have endeavoured, in several of my Papers, to revive that way of Writing, and hope I have not been altogether unsuccessful in it; for I find there is always a great Demand for those particular Papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviving allegorical writing is recommended as it has high precedents and a public appetite; allegory can be an effective vehicle for moral and satirical points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fiction/dream to satirize safely
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Story on which it is built does Honour to the Sex, and that in order to abuse them, the Writer is obliged to have recourse to Dream and Fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When lampooning or railling against social subjects (e.g., marriage, women), grounding satire in dream or fiction distances the attack from factual slander and allows freer raillery without (claimed) offense — a rhetorical device to protect author and lend comic license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat family government as moral/political training
rubrics_metrics.description: I look upon my Family as a Patriarchal Sovereignty, in which I am my self both King and Priest. All great Governments are nothing else but Clusters of these little private Royalties ... I am perpetually taken up in giving out Orders, in prescribing Duties, in hearing Parties, in administring Justice, and in distributing Rewards and Punishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents should exercise just authority, give virtuous education, set industry and honest principles to cultivate children who may prosper in public life; large families can be a means to 'raise a family' across professions if governed properly.
